what_expression.description: A [DataPrime](https://coralogix.com/docs/dataprime-query-language/) expression that filters which **group-by values** to suppress within the selected alerts. The expression must start with `source logs | filter` (this syntax is required even for metric or tracing alerts - the filtering works on group-by values regardless of alert type). Use `"source logs | filter true"` to suppress all alert activity without filtering specific values. Use `"source logs | filter $d.fieldName == 'value'"` to suppress only when specific group-by values match. This field controls **what triggered values** to suppress, while `alerts_unique_ids` or `meta_labels` control **which alerts** the rule applies to.

filter.description: Alert Scheduler filter. Only one of `meta_labels` or `alerts_unique_ids` can be set. If none of them set, all alerts will be affected.

what_expression.description: A [DataPrime](https://coralogix.com/docs/dataprime-query-language/) expression that filters which **group-by values** to suppress within the selected alerts. The expression must start with `source logs | filter` (this syntax is required even for metric or tracing alerts - the filtering works on group-by values regardless of alert type). Use `"source logs | filter true"` to suppress all alert activity without filtering specific values. Use `"source logs | filter $d.fieldName == 'value'"` to suppress only when specific group-by values match. This field controls **what triggered values** to suppress, while `alerts_unique_ids` or `meta_labels` control **which alerts** the rule applies to.

filter.description: Alert Scheduler filter. Only one of `meta_labels` or `alerts_unique_ids` can be set. If none of them set, all alerts will be affected.

for_over.description: The number of time units to wait before the alert is triggered. For example, if the frequency is set to `hours` and the value is set to `2`, the alert will be triggered after 2 hours.

frequency.description: The time unit to wait before the alert is triggered. Can be `minutes`, `hours` or `days`.

duration.description: The duration from the start time to wait.

end_time.description: The end time of the time frame. In a isodate format. For example, `2021-01-01T00:00:00.000`.

time_zone.description: Timezone (e.g. `UTC`, `UTC+0`, `UTC+2`). Both `UTC` and `UTC+0` are accepted for zero offset.

operation.description: The operation to perform. Can be `mute` or `active`.

always_active.description: When set to `true`, creates a permanent suppression rule that is always active. This is mutually exclusive with `dynamic`. When using `always_active = true`, no time frame or frequency configuration is needed.

for_over.description: The number of time units to wait before the alert is triggered. For example, if the frequency is set to `hours` and the value is set to `2`, the alert will be triggered after 2 hours.

duration.description: The duration from the start time to wait.

end_time.description: The end time of the time frame. In a isodate format. For example, `2021-01-01T00:00:00.000`.

time_zone.description: Timezone (e.g. `UTC`, `UTC+0`, `UTC+2`). Both `UTC` and `UTC+0` are accepted for zero offset.

recurring.description: Recurring schedule configuration. Use `dynamic` for time-based recurring schedules, or `always_active = true` for permanent suppression rules.

schedule.description: Exactly one of `one_time` or `recurring` must be set.

default_expression.description: Default expression to use when no filter matches the query. Until further notice, this is limited to `true` (everything is included) or `false` (nothing is included). Use a version tag (e.g `<v1>true` or `<v1>false`)

entity_type.description: Entity type to apply the expression on

filters.description: Filters applied to include data in the scope.

block.description: Coralogix Scope. Scopes assign data access to users via groups. For more info please review - https://coralogix.com/docs/user-guides/account-management/user-management/scopes/.

compare_type.description: Compare type. This is the compare type of the SLO. Valid values are: ["ends_with" "includes" "is" "starts_with" "unspecified"]

period.description: Period. This is the period of the SLO. Valid values are: ["14_days" "30_days" "7_days" "unspecified"]

service_name.description: Service name. This is the name of the service that the SLO is associated with.

target_percentage.description: Target percentage. This is the target percentage of the SLO.

threshold_microseconds.description: Threshold in microseconds. Required when `type` is `latency`.

threshold_symbol_type.description: Threshold symbol type. Required when `type` is `latency`. Valid values are: ["equal" "greater" "greater_or_equal" "less" "less_or_equal"]

type.description: Type. This is the type of the SLO. Valid values are: "error", "latency".

block.description: Coralogix SLO. For more info please review - https://coralogix.com/docs/user-guides/apm/features/service-slos/.

labels.description: List of labels to group SLO evaluations by.
Optional map of labels to attach to the SLO.

comparison_operator.description: Comparison operator used to evaluate the threshold. One of: greater_than,greater_than_or_equals,less_than,less_than_or_equals,unspecified

query.description: Query used for evaluating the time-window SLI.

window.description: Time window type for evaluation. One of: 1_minute, 5_minutes, unspecified.

sli.description: SLI definition: exactly one of request_based_metric_sli or window_based_metric_sli must be provided.

slo_time_frame.description: SLO time window. One of: 14_days, 21_days, 28_days, 7_days, unspecified.

window.description: SLO time window. One of: 14_days, 21_days, 28_days, 7_days, unspecified.

block.description: Coralogix New SLO. Read more about limits and details at https://coralogix.com/docs/user-guides/slos/introduction/

rule_type.description: The rule type. Can be one of ["includes" "is" "is_not" "starts_with" "unspecified"].

applications.description: The applications to apply the policy on. Applies the policy on all the applications by default.

archive_retention_id.description: Allowing logs with a specific retention to be tagged.

dpxl_expression.description: DataPrime expression to match logs for this policy. Mutually exclusive with `severities` — set exactly one. The expression must include a version prefix, e.g. `<v1> $d.severity == 'INFO'`.

enabled.description: Determines weather the policy will be enabled. True by default.

order.description: The policy's order between the other policies.

priority.description: The policy priority. Can be one of ["block" "high" "low" "medium"].

daily_quota_percentage.description: Daily quota consumption (in percent) at which this tier becomes active. Must be between 0 and 100.

priority.description: The priority to apply when this tier is active. Can be one of ["block" "high" "low" "medium"].

usage_tiers.description: Ordered list of quota-consumption tiers; the policy's priority is dynamically reassigned to the matching tier's `priority` once `daily_quota_percentage` is reached.

quota_based_priority_override.description: Dynamically reassign the policy's priority based on daily quota consumption tiers.

severities.description: The severities to apply the policy on. Valid severities are ["critical" "debug" "error" "info" "verbose" "warning"].

subsystems.description: The subsystems to apply the policy on. Applies the policy on all the subsystems by default.

block.description: Coralogix TCO-Policies-List. For more information - https://coralogix.com/docs/tco-optimizer-api.

actions.description: The actions to apply the policy on. Applies the policy on all the actions by default.

tags.description: The tags to apply the policy on. Applies the policy on all the tags by default.

user_name.description: User name (email). Comparison is case-insensitive: SSO login can normalize letter case in the backend, and that normalization will not trigger drift in subsequent plans.

block.description: Coralogix User. For more info please review - https://coralogix.com/docs/user-guides/account-management/user-management/manage-team-members/.

headers.description: Webhook headers. Map of string to string.

method.description: Webhook method. can be one of: get, post, put

detail.description: Event bridge message. JSON string. More details about the token ["here"](https://coralogix.com/docs/user-guides/alerting/outbound-webhooks/generic-outbound-webhooks-alert-webhooks/#placeholders)

detail_type.description: Free text to be included in the event.

event_bus_arn.description: Corresponds to the event bus, which will receive notifications. The policy attached must contain permission to publish.

role_name.description: Corresponds to the AWS IAM role that will be created in your account.

source.description: Free text is used to identify the messages Coralogix sends.

external_id.description: Webhook external ID. Using to linq webhook to alert.

microsoft_teams.description: Microsoft Teams webhook. (Deprecated, please use microsoft_teams_workflow)

url.description: Webhook URL returned by the service when present. SendLog webhooks do not support configuring a URL.

active.description: Determines if the attachment is active. Default is true.

type.description: Slack attachment type. can be one of: empty, logs, metric_snapshot

notify_on.description: Slack notifications. can be one of: data_usage, error_and_critical_logs, flow_anomalies, spike_anomalies
